seo.title: Mykael Sicard - Full-Stack Developer
seo.description: Full-stack developer in New York. Production experience owning complex systems end to end, from PostgreSQL schema design and REST APIs to React and Next.js frontends.

summary: Hi, I'm Mykael, a full-stack developer in New York City with 2+ years shipping production features across TypeScript, React, Next.js, Python, and PostgreSQL. At a social content platform I owned a compliance system end to end, from schema design to APIs and an admin dashboard, rebuilt video encoding as a BullMQ/Redis job pipeline, and extended Stream Chat with custom monetization. I'm AWS Certified Cloud Practitioner and Microsoft Certified in Azure AI, and I build my own projects end to end too, including Formalytx, an F1 telemetry explorer built with Next.js, FastAPI, and Cloudflare R2. I'm currently studying computer science at BMCC and looking for my next full-stack or backend role, and outside of work I game and stay active in the gym.

bullets: Diagnosed a connectivity failure between Windows-hosted PostgreSQL and WSL-based applications by reconfiguring listener bindings and host-based authentication rules; resolved it one-on-one for 4 affected students and documented the fix in a setup guide that preempted an estimated 19 more.

Led 3 student teams (3-5 members each) through 3-week capstones, assigning tickets and tracking progress in GitHub Projects; ran standups with all 7 teams to surface blockers, with all 3 led teams delivering on time.

Rebuilt video encoding as a BullMQ/Redis job pipeline with bounded concurrency and retries, taking 10 simultaneous uploads from 5 completed to 10 and cutting worst API latency from 1.8s to 47ms in benchmarks.

Built the platform's compliance system end-to-end (age verification, review queue, appeals, admin dashboard) to meet regulatory requirements, owning the PostgreSQL schema, Encore.dev review APIs, and admin UI; restricted search so only approved content reached users.

Extended the Stream Chat SDK with custom monetization (per-user message rates, per-media pricing) and cut connection handshakes ~92% (12 to 1 per session) by moving to a single app-level client gated on account status.
Replaced the Plyr/hls.js player with a shared Video.js component across 6 video surfaces, fixing a background-download leak and an early-click race while cutting first-load JS by 8.7%.

projects.name: Formalytx
projects.summary: An F1 telemetry explorer - browse seasons, sessions, and driver laps, and visualize raw car telemetry.
overview: Formalytx is a Formula 1 telemetry explorer that lets users navigate F1 seasons, events, and sessions - then dive into driver laps and raw car telemetry, all in one place. Pick a year and event, choose a session, select drivers to compare, and plot lap times and telemetry channels like speed, throttle, and brake.

The frontend is built with Next.js 16 (App Router), React 19, and TypeScript, styled with Tailwind CSS and shadcn/ui, with ECharts powering the interactive telemetry visualizations and TanStack Query handling data fetching and caching. The backend is a FastAPI service written in Python exposing 9 typed REST endpoints, with the frontend on Vercel and the API on Railway.

Loading sessions on demand through FastF1 was too slow for real users, so I replaced it with a per-lap archive in Cloudflare R2 covering 961 sessions, 538k laps, and 5.3 GB. Real-user p95 latency on uncached requests fell from 11.8s to 0.68s and gateway timeouts disappeared. A Railway cron job keeps the archive current, exporting each session to R2 within 15 minutes of it ending and re-checking for 2 days to catch steward penalties, writing only the objects that changed.

As the sole developer, I design, build, and operate the entire stack. When requests started stalling for 30 seconds, I traced it through Railway flow logs to idle R2 connections being dropped in transit, and fixed it with TCP keepalive on the boto3 connection pool, cutting p99 latency from 31s to 0.86s. The explorer now serves around 120 unique visitors a month.

As a Formula 1 fan, this project was a true passion build. Combining my love for the sport with full-stack engineering made every part of the process rewarding, and seeing real race data come to life in the explorer is something I'm genuinely proud of.

projects.name: Buddy Walk
projects.summary: A trial-evaluation dashboard for an assistive navigation app for blind and low-vision travelers.
overview: Buddy Walk is an assistive navigation app for blind and low-vision travelers, a React Native (Expo) client backed by a Node.js and Express API, developed by a research team at the Borough of Manhattan Community College. I joined as a CSTEP Research Scholar in Fall 2026 to build the tooling the team uses to evaluate its last-meters guidance in the field.

I built a trial-evaluation dashboard, served by the Express API and backed by MongoDB, that shows GPS accuracy, the resolved destination, the Street View panorama, and the outcome for every field test, with filters so the team can compare localization methods side by side.

I also implemented a retry workflow that reruns past test trials through the OpenAI and Street View pipeline, up to 3 at once, with UUIDv7 idempotency keys, lease renewal, and an admin-token gate. Retries are excluded from the evaluation sample, so rerunning a trial never skews the results the team is measuring.
